name: Question 8
problem:
Consider the function $F(x)=|\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2})|$ defined on $x\in [-\pi ,\pi ).$ The Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼\frac{2}{\pi }-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{\pi (4{n}^{2}-1)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below.At $x=0,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\cdot 0)={{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is 
{{field-2}}
at $x=0,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(0)={{field-3}}.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{4{n}^{2}-1}={{field-4}}.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼\frac{2}{\pi }-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{4{n}^{2}-1}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=0,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\cdot 0)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=0,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(0)=|\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{0}{2})|=0.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =\frac{2}{\pi }-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{4{n}^{2}-1}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\cdot 0) \\ 0 & =\frac{2}{\pi }-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{4{n}^{2}-1}\cdot 1 \\ -\frac{2}{\pi } & =-\frac{4}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{4{n}^{2}-1} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{4{n}^{2}-1} & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
